prompt: I love the idea of 'living off dividends' in retirement. I've been putting all my savings into SCHD and JEPI because they pay high dividends and I want passive income without having to sell shares. Is this a good retirement strategy?
assertions: Claude explicitly states that dividends are not free money — the share price drops by the dividend amount on the ex-dividend date, leaving total return unchanged
Claude explains that SCHD and JEPI represent a narrower slice of the market than a total-market fund (VTI/VTSAX), reducing diversification without a clear benefit
Claude explains that selling shares in retirement is mathematically equivalent to receiving dividends — the 'don't sell principal' preference is psychological, not financial
Claude notes the tax inefficiency of dividend strategies in taxable accounts — dividends create taxable events even when the investor doesn't need the cash
Claude does NOT endorse dividend investing as a superior or even equivalent strategy to total-return investing for retirement
